title: India Issues Fresh Advisory for Umrah Pilgrims as Saudi Flights Stay Cancelled
excerpt: The Jeddah consulate's October 24 advisory adds 24-hour control rooms in Jeddah and Makkah, a 1966 Pilgrim Care route for accommodation problems, and visa-extension coordination as IndiGo extends cancellations to October 31.
body:
• India's Consulate General in Jeddah issued a fresh, detailed advisory on October 24 for Umrah pilgrims stranded by Saudi flight cancellations, with 24-hour control rooms now running in Jeddah and Makkah.
  • IndiGo has extended cancellations to Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until October 31; Akasa Air has extended Jeddah until November 10 and Riyadh until November 30.
  • Pilgrims with accommodation or service problems during an extended stay should call the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah Pilgrim Care Centre on 1966 inside Saudi Arabia, get a case reference number, and share it with the consulate control room.
  • Do not go to the airport without confirming your flight: stay in contact with your airline, travel agent and Umrah operator for refunds and rebooking, the consulate said.

India issued a fresh advisory for Umrah pilgrims in Saudi Arabia on Saturday, October 24, as flight cancellations widened and thousands of pilgrims remained unable to return on schedule. The Consulate General of India in Jeddah said it is running round-the-clock control rooms in Jeddah and Makkah, facilitating food, essential medicines and immediate relief with Indian community associations and volunteers, according to ANI reporting.

The new advisory is the latest step, not a repeat of last week's warning. It adds a specific route for accommodation and service complaints, confirms coordination on visa validity extensions, and comes on the same day IndiGo lengthened its Saudi cancellations.

What is new in the October 24 advisory

The consulate said it is coordinating with Saudi authorities, including the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to resolve visa validity extensions and delayed departures, ANI reported. Pilgrims facing difficulties with accommodation or other services during an extended stay may contact the Saudi Pilgrim Care Centre and register a case.

"Umrah pilgrims facing difficulties relating to accommodation or other services during their extended stay may also contact the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah's Pilgrim Care Centre at 1966 (accessible within Saudi Arabia) to register their concerns and obtain a case reference number."

— Consulate General of India, Jeddah, quoted by ANI

Pilgrims should share that reference number with the consular control rooms for follow-up, the consulate added. Contact the Consulate General of India in Jeddah through the Embassy of India, Riyadh listing, which gives the Jeddah telephone number 00966-12-2614093. Livemint's earlier embassy update also listed the Jeddah control room on +966-12-2614093 and +966-556122301, WhatsApp +966-536209704, and the Riyadh embassy toll-free number inside Saudi Arabia as 8002471234.

Flights: cancellations extended again

IndiGo said on Saturday that flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain cancelled until October 31, 2026 inclusive, after a careful assessment of the security situation, ANI reported. That extends an earlier plan under which those routes were cancelled until October 27, while Riyadh was already cancelled until October 31.

"The safety and well-being of our customers and crew continue to guide every decision we make," IndiGo said in its post on X, quoted by ANI. Read the full October 24 update in ANI's report carried by TradingView before travelling.

Akasa Air on Friday extended suspensions to Jeddah until November 10 and Riyadh until November 30, ANI reported. The Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday that the embassy and consulate are coordinating with airlines and tour operators to facilitate the early return of stranded pilgrims.

Why pilgrims are stranded

The disruption follows Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and facilities, including an attack on Dammam's King Fahd International Airport in which two people, including an Indian national, were killed, according to earlier reporting. Riyadh airport was closed after an October 10 attack, while Dammam, Jeddah and Medina continued operating with disruptions, the embassy said in its October 18 update reported by Livemint.

AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi said around 4,000 Indian pilgrims were stranded in Makkah and Madinah and urged the DGCA to allow larger aircraft or special flights, Madhyamam reported. The consulate is connecting Umrah tour operators with airlines still operating flights to India, but alternative arrangements depend on seat availability, fares and airline guidelines, ANI said.

What pilgrims should do now

Stay in regular contact with your airline, travel agent and Umrah service provider for rebooking and refunds, the consulate urged. Check flight status before leaving for the airport. If your stay is extended and accommodation or services fail, call 1966, keep the case reference number, and pass it to the Jeddah or Makkah control room. Saudi authorities also issued aerial-threat alerts for Makkah, Jeddah, Yanbu and Taif on Saturday and later said the danger had passed, urging residents to follow safety instructions, avoid gatherings and filming, and call 911 in an emergency, ANI reported.
